input: Primary shortest-path domain: grid is a nonempty square n by n binary integer array with n distinct mutable row objects. Zero means open and one means blocked. Total n * n must fit the shared collection-size bound. Separate predecessor-effect compatibility domain: rows may instead repeat references to the same mutable row object; this retains mutation-driven traversal behavior but does not promise shortest-path correctness on an independent-cell interpretation of the original matrix. All input collections are ordinary finite dense arrays/lists, not subclasses, proxies, sparse arrays or accessor-backed collections; node fields, where present, are plain data fields. Strings are ordinary/primitive strings. There is no concurrent mutation or monkey-patching of standard built-ins. Every individual collection length, computed storage count and index fits [0, 4294967295], except explicit -1 sentinels. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Actual allocation/resource capacity and completion remain qualification obligations, not guarantees from these declared bounds. Python integers are plain int values, excluding bool; node identity keys, when used, are opaque id values.
return: On the primary distinct-row domain, the integer minimum number of cells on an initially open eight-neighbor path from upper-left to lower-right, counting both endpoints, or -1 when no such path exists. An open 1 by 1 grid returns 1. On the aliased-row compatibility domain, the result is the distance attached to the first dequeued target, or -1 if none is dequeued, under the specified mutation-driven traversal; alias-propagated marking can suppress cells that were initially zero.
mutation_aliasing: Intentionally mutates the exact input grid in place: if the start is blocked, returns -1 without writes; otherwise marks grid[0][0] = 1 before enqueue. On each FIFO dequeue, returns immediately if that cell is the target; otherwise examines eight neighbors in row-major order and sets each currently zero in-bounds cell to 1 before enqueue. It does not reject a blocked target early, so unsuccessful searches still mark reachable cells. Original outer and row identities, lengths, and all initial ones remain unchanged. Caller aliases observe writes; repeated row references propagate a write to every aliased row position, and subsequent discovery uses those propagated values. The Solution object retains no state.
numeric: Coordinates stay within one step of [0, n - 1] before bounds checks. Each coordinate can be enqueued at most once because values only change from zero to one. Distances are at most n * n, and all count/index arithmetic is exact. All integer inputs and computed mathematical counts remain within [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991]. No bitwise coercion is used.
complexity: O(n^2 + 1) worst-case time and O(n^2 + 1) auxiliary space on both declared domains. Each coordinate is enqueued at most once and expanded with eight candidate neighbors; input-cell marking replaces a separate visited matrix. The head-cursor queue retains processed coordinate/distance triples and its full storage is counted. Bounds use bounded-word arithmetic, constant-time array indexing and amortized append; built-in allocation costs are included.
